title: What the ledger claims — 8 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
What the ledger claims. 8 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/ledgerclaims.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 3 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 5 pairs; the theorems fall into 4 strands, the largest of 3. Most binding: rounds (3), saving (2), addr4 (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: merkle.lean. Built on it: speed.lean. Checking this cluster needs 4 files: src/proof/ledgerclaims.lean, src/proof/address.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean, src/proof/merkle.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to ca6ad553-fa5e-854d-8d19-3c2829bfe6cd. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (7, 8, 0, 6, 7, 1, 2). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: demand3.lean (3 observed, 1.3 expected, lift 2.3), elementary.lean (5 observed, 2.75 expected, lift 1.82), imagined.lean (12 observed, 8.1 expected, lift 1.48). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 3.12 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 80.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 14.79; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.62. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 8f0ad88d7a67 (2026-09-15), over 817 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. membership_grows_by_one_seal_per_doubling and membership_is_logarithmic_not_linear restate the O(log n) membership proof of a hash tree — Ralph Merkle, 1979 (thesis); CRYPTO 1987 — which merkle.lean in this same deposit already credits. Classified unbounded on the ground that the subject is this deposit's own ledger; the ledger is its own, the logarithm is not. Bounded: what is not prior art is what THIS ledger claims — the 967-receipt case, the saving arithmetic, and the 128-bit seal width as this deposit mints it. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. a_seal_is_128_bits — (toUuidBytes [97]).length * 8 = 128 record
  2. membership_grows_by_one_seal_per_doubling — rounds 40 2 = 1 ∧ rounds 40 4 = 2 ∧ rounds 40 8 = 3 ∧ rounds 40 16 = 4 ∧ rounds 40 32 = 5 ∧ rounds 40 64 = 6 ∧ rounds 40 128 = 7 ∧ rounds 40 256 = 8 record
  3. membership_is_logarithmic_not_linear — rounds 40 1024 = 10 ∧ rounds 40 1024 < 1024 ∧ rounds 40 1024 * 128 < 1024 * 128 record
  4. the_967_receipt_case — saving 967 20 = 947 ∧ 20 + 947 = 967 record
  5. a_saving_never_exceeds_its_value — (List.range 40).all (fun v => (List.range 40).all (fun w => saving v w ≤ v)) record
  6. more_payloads_than_addresses_must_collide — ((List.range 17).map addr4).eraseDups.length < 17 record
  7. the_address_does_not_determine_the_payload — ((List.range 17).any (fun a => (List.range 17).any (fun b => a != b && addr4 a == addr4 b))) = true record
  8. a_proof_is_smaller_than_its_set_across_the_octave — (List.range' 2 255).all (fun n => rounds 40 n < n) record

Recompute. Clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions at commit 8f0ad88d7a67 and run npm ci && npm run lean, which checks every Lean file in dependency order. This record was generated by scripts/clusters.ts from the source and the ledger.
